I farm here in Iringa and this plot of about 0.84 hectares is mine, intercropped like I always do. I went to school a bit but I farm the way my father did — I watch my neighbors and I do not spend money I do not have. This season the rains look normal so I will do mostly what I did last year. I keep cattle and goats so I have manure from the boma, and I will carry some to this plot before planting. Fertilizer from the shop is expensive and one bag is a lot of money, but here in Iringa many of us put a little urea on the maize when it is knee-high if cash allows — I will buy one bag and stretch it across my plots, so this plot gets only a small share. For seed, I save my own from last harvest for the intercrop, but for the maize I will buy a small tin of improved seed because my neighbor got a good harvest from it last year. I do not spray — pesticides cost too much and I pick off pests by hand. No irrigation here, we depend on the rain. The work is done by me, my wife and my older children, and at weeding and harvest I will call a few neighbors and pay them with food or a little cash.
